literal: Poverty's affliction having begged we will end saying than the hardness hard-natured thing there is not.
translation: There is no hardness greater than the hard-hearted ignorance of saying, 'We will cure the affliction of poverty by begging.'
modern: வறுமையின் துன்பத்தைப் பிச்சை எடுத்துத் தீர்ப்போம் என்று சொல்லும் வன்மையை விடக் கொடிய வன்மை வேறு இல்லை.
explanation: This couplet condemns the mindset of choosing to beg as a solution to poverty. The word inmai refers to poverty, and iṭumpai is the sorrow it brings. The poet states that resolving to cure this sorrow by begging shows a stubborn ignorance or hardness of heart. There is absolutely nothing harder or worse than this degrading resolution.
